Layout and sizes of pagemap entries, scan argument and region records, and walk structures.

findings.text: The dossier exposes open, read and release handlers for the pagemap view. Open binds the target address space after a read-mode permission check and fails when the target is gone. Read streams fixed-size entries indexed by file offset and advances the offset by bytes delivered. Release drops the held reference when present.

Each pagemap entry combines presence, swap, file backing, soft dirtiness, userfault write protection, guard marking and exclusivity into a flag word plus a frame number. VMA level soft dirtiness is always folded in. File versus anonymous and exclusive-mapping determinations derive from the underlying folio when a page is available.

Whether frame numbers carry real location data is gated by privilege. Unprivileged readers observe zeroed frames while still observing status flags. Privileged swap frames encode type and offset with a fixed shift, and present frames encode page frame numbers with per-page stepping.

A single transparent huge mapping is reported as a sequence of base-page entries sharing most flags. The starting subpage index derives from the address position inside the huge range, and successive entries advance the frame value according to present or swap kind until the requested end.

Pagemap table traversal holds exactly one leaf lock at a time. The transparent huge attempt takes its dedicated lock and releases it before returning. The small-page path maps and locks the table, iterates, then unmaps and unlocks. The hugeTLB path holds its dedicated lock across sampling and emission. Each leaf handler yields the processor after dropping its lock.

The walk dispatch table routes middle-level entries to the middle handler, holes to a hole handler, and hugeTLB entries to a huge handler, under a read-mode walk lock. When hugeTLB support is absent the huge hook is null and that case is not visited.

Read validates alignment of offset and length, rejects disclosure beyond the task size, defends against arithmetic wrap, normalizes tagged addresses under a killable read lock, walks the range in fixed-size chunks each under a fresh read lock, and treats a full internal buffer as successful partial completion while copying only the filled prefix to user space.

The scan category universe is the union of write-allowed, written, file, present, swapped, zero page, huge, soft-dirty, guard and accessed bits. Masks referencing bits outside this set are not part of the shown contract.
Scan control accepts exactly the write-protect-matching request and the strict async-capability check request. No other flag bits are recognized in the shown fragments.

Scan state carries the user argument block, a precomputed mask of categories requiring extra work, the current VMA contribution, a kernel staging vector with length and cursor, a found-page counter, and the user destination pointer.

Base-page classification distinguishes empty, present and swapped table contents. Empty entries report written status only on write-tracking VMAs. Present and swapped entries add written or accessed marks only when the corresponding protection mark is absent and the VMA enables that tracking, plus file, zero, soft-dirty or guard attributes as applicable.

Large-page classification always includes the huge marker. Empty large entries report only that marker, while populated or swapped large entries add the same present versus swapped family of marks as base pages, with file backing and zero detection adapted to large-page helpers and swapped hugeTLB file checks omitted.

Page acceptance applies inversion before masking, requires all must-match bits, and requires a non-empty intersection when an any-of mask is supplied. VMA prefiltering applies only to the write-allowed bit with the same inversion, and VMAs lacking async write-tracking either fail strictly, are skipped when protection was requested, or are walked when protection is not involved.

Matching ranges are coalesced when contiguous and identically categorized, otherwise appended until the staging vector fills. Total found pages are checked for overflow and capped at a user maximum with truncation, end adjustment and a no-space signal that still records progress. A backout helper shortens or clears the trailing range and subtracts its pages.

Write-protection on match arms the userfault mark appropriate to each table level, using marker entries for empty slots and ignoring poison or existing marker huge entries. Callers flush only the span actually armed. A partially covered transparent huge page is split and rescanned as small pages, while a partially covered hugeTLB page is backed out and reported as stopping at its start.

Scan leaf handlers serialize against table mutation with the level-appropriate lock. Transparent huge and small-page paths hold their leaf lock across classification and optional arming, with small-page arming batched under lazy mode. The hugeTLB arming path additionally holds the mapping write lock, while the non-arming hugeTLB fast path samples without acquiring the shown write or leaf locks.

Pagemap reading moves from offset validation through chunked walks to user copy, advancing the virtual cursor to each chunk end and the file offset by bytes copied, stopping at task end, request exhaustion or error. Scanning moves per VMA from test to leaf classification to staged output, with walk end recording the truncation or partial-huge stop point.

Frame disclosure without privilege gating would expose physical layout; the shown code gates it per open file. Unchecked offset arithmetic could wrap past task size, and unchecked found-page accumulation could overflow; the shown code clamps ranges and checks addition. Skipped frame-map VMAs, strict async enforcement, and partial large-page handling prevent silent misprotection or misreporting.
